# Built 2026-08-13 by the P-M2a lane from the per-subdir MANIFEST.tsv publication_lag fields (manifest_source names the exact file), DATA_INVENTORY.md §3/§4b and D-057 itself. Referenced from DATA_INVENTORY.md §4c.

# REVISED 2026-08-14 by THE ONE D-001 FIX PASS (availability sub-lane) closing R79/R39, R82, R83, R84, R85, R86 and R14. What changed is stated per rule below; the code is engine/port_m2/availability.py and the red-first tests are engine/port_m2/test_avail_fixlane.py.

# LAW (D-057 / PORT_M2_SHEETS_SPEC.md §2): a series joins on availability_ts = f(stamp_date), never on its stamp date. The sheet builder's guard enforces availability_ts < decision_ts (strict; the pinned reading of "availability_ts <= decision_ts, never equal-time", see engine/port_m2/m2_common.py CausalGuard.avail).
# CALENDARS (both DERIVED from banked data; no hand-written holiday list exists anywhere in the program):
#   US MARKET/TREASURY  observation dates of port_context/fred_refresh/FRED_DGS10.csv carrying a numeric value.

#   US FEDERAL/AGENCY   observation dates of port_context/FRED_DTWEXBGS.csv carrying a numeric value. DTWEXBGS is the Federal Reserve Board's own H.10 index, so a blank IS a Board closure. Verified 2021-2025: the 55 weekday blanks are the federal holidays plus 2021-01-20 (Inauguration Day), 2021-12-31 and 2023-11-10 (observed holidays). R85: three of those 55 are TREASURY business days, so agency rules must NOT use the Treasury calendar — 2023-11-10 is a Friday, i.e. a COT release day.
# avail_rule vocabulary (implemented in engine/port_m2/availability.py, one function per rule, red-first fixtures in engine/port_m2/leakfix.py + test_avail_fixlane.py):

#   NEXT_US_BD        17:00 America/New_York of the first US FEDERAL business day STRICTLY AFTER stamp_date. R83/R84: this is D-057's conservative default read literally as "the next FULL trading day" — 17:00 ET is the CME close, the instant that day is complete. The pre-fix rule used 00:00 ET (= 04:00/05:00 UTC), which sits inside the m0 TOKYO phase and before all of LONDON, so a d+1 London decision read a value FRED had not posted (~10h/series/day). The calendar is the FEDERAL one because every series carrying this rule except GOLD_SILVER_RATIO is published BY FRED, which does not post on a federal holiday; for GOLD_SILVER_RATIO the federal calendar is the more conservative of the two.

#   H10_NEXT_MONDAY   16:15 America/New_York of the first Monday STRICTLY AFTER stamp_date, advanced to the next FEDERAL business day if that Monday is a federal holiday (R82: 34 such Mondays in 2021-2025, incl. 2022-01-17 / 02-21 / 05-30 / 06-20 / 07-04 inside E2).

#   COT_FRI_1530ET    15:30 America/New_York of the FRIDAY OF THE STAMP'S OWN WEEK, delayed to the next FEDERAL business day when any weekday of that Mon-Fri week is a federal closure — the CFTC's stated holiday-week rule. R79/R39: the pre-fix rule was stamp_date + 3 CALENDAR days with no holiday adjustment, which asserted publication on 6 non-business days in 2021-2025 (2021-12-24, 2022-04-15, 2022-11-11, 2024-03-29, 2025-04-18, 2025-07-04), ignored the delay in ~55 report weeks (5 in E2), and computed a THURSDAY release for the 508 MONDAY-stamped rows (report dates 2023-07-03, 2025-11-10).
#   NEXT_JST_BD_1500  15:00 Asia/Tokyo of the first JGB business day STRICTLY AFTER stamp_date ("next JST afternoon", D-057). JST business days are read from JGB_yields_all.csv observation dates.
#   NEXT_JST_BD_0000  00:00 Asia/Tokyo of the first JST business day STRICTLY AFTER stamp_date.

#   NEXT_CN_BD_0000   00:00 Asia/Shanghai of the first Mon-Fri weekday STRICTLY AFTER stamp_date (no long CN daily calendar is banked; the weekday rule is conservative for a Friday-stamped weekly series).

#   SCHEDULE_EXEMPT   no lag arithmetic — the dates are announced months ahead (D-057 exempts scheduled calendars). The EVENT fires at its own scheduled clock; the sheet shows only the NEXT release strictly after decision_ts plus a countdown.

# CALENDAR EXHAUSTION (R86): a stamp past the end of its calendar yields availability.CALENDAR_EXHAUSTED — a refusal VALUE that is counted on the series (n_refused) and makes latest() REFUSE. It is never dropped, and a stale older observation is never served in its place.
# UNKNOWN LAG DEFAULT (D-057): NEXT_US_BD for US-published series, NEXT_JST_BD_0000 for JP, NEXT_CN_BD_0000 for CN. Every row below states which rule it uses and why; no row is defaulted silently.

# VINTAGE (R14): publication_fact documents FIRST-PRINT timing, but the banked files hold the LATEST vintage of every series and no vintage archive exists for any of them. vintage_class therefore declares, per series, whether the joined value is the one that was published at availability_ts (FIRST_PRINT) or may be a later correction of it (REVISED_VALUE). D-057 is satisfied in form for a REVISED_VALUE row and NOT in substance; the flag rides on every availability.AvailSeries.latest() answer so S12 declares the limitation instead of leaving it silent. SCHEDULE = a calendar row (dates, not values).
